text: A claimant working part-time while certifying availability for full-time work must report all gross earnings for the certification week, regardless of when payment is received.
Claims flagged for identity-verification mismatch must be placed in pending status and are not payable until the claimant completes in-person or notarized identity confirmation.

A shared IP address or device alone is not sufficient grounds for a fraud determination; investigators must corroborate with at least one additional independent signal before referring a case for adjudication.
An overpayment resulting from agency error, where the claimant neither knew nor reasonably should have known the payment was in error, may be eligible for waiver upon request.

Claims where the claimant's employment history spans multiple states must be adjudicated under the paying state's law, with wage records requested from all states of employment before a determination is issued.
A claimant determined ineligible due to a fraud finding has the right to appeal within 20 calendar days of the determination notice; benefits remain suspended pending the appeal outcome.

IP-based signals (shared IP, geolocation mismatch, sequential IP clustering) should be treated as investigative leads, not standalone proof; VPN and mobile carrier NAT usage produce legitimate false positives.
When a new case shares two or more signals with a previously confirmed-fraud case, investigators should review the prior case's full disposition notes before drafting a new determination.
